correctness.rationale: Newton identities and unit-modulus self-inversive symmetry force the six-root polynomial to have only z^6,z^3,constant terms, hence two disjoint equilateral triples; this also proves 3-,4-,5-node rigidity. For 0<beta<2pi/3 the paired tangent edges close, have strictly positive forward turns, and bound a convex equal-edge polygon. Direct shoelace gives A=sqrt(3)*ell^2*(1+2*cos(beta-pi/3))/2. The third harmonic mu=|cos(3beta/2)| has inverse |beta-pi/3|=(2/3)arcsin(mu). The exact deficit D=2sqrt(3)*ell^2*sin^2((arcsin(mu))/3) and triple-angle factor give the sharp 2sqrt(3)/9 and sqrt(3)/2 coefficients, with the latter only approached as mu tends to 1; area range open at the collapsing lower end.
